solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Feeling love in little ways

indicators.note: in tells us the word for love goes inside the little ways

parts.note: paths are little ways or tracks
love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone shows affection through small daily gestures.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathos is the quality that stirs pity or sad emotion, a kind of feeling.

clue.text: Sad pair, having erred, originally evicted here

definitions.text: Sad pair, having erred, originally evicted here

indicators.note: having erred means having gone astray, so these letters wander into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Adam and Eve, sorrowful after their sin, were thrown out of Eden.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the sinning couple were expelled from Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is the Garden of Eden, from which Adam and Eve were expelled after the Fall.

clue.text: Wealth of much loved person

definitions.meaning: riches or valuables, gold and jewels hoarded up
a dear, precious one, as in 'you are a real gem'

explanation.surface: The riches belonging to a darling.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure means hoarded riches and also a cherished person.

clue.text: Outstanding poem that's recited

indicators.note: something recited is spoken out, so we want a word that matches its pronunciation

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: An excellent poem read aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt that is outstanding is still due, unpaid.

clue.text: Said to be celebrated

definitions.meaning: to have ... something is to have remarked or commented it
a festival is ... when it is kept or marked

explanation.surface: Something reported as having been honoured.
explanation.definitionFit: Observed means both remarked aloud and kept, as one keeps a holiday or anniversary.

clue.text: Manoeuvring of the bankers or philanderers may produce them

indicators.note: manoeuvring moves things about, so these letters are repositioned

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Schemes by financiers or womanisers may cause grief.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearts shattered by grief from love betrayed are what faithless lovers leave behind.

clue.text: Dines in style at smart restaurants

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone takes meals elegantly at chic restaurants.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat is to have a meal, so eats matches dines.

clue.text: Such a threat is hardly barefaced

definitions.text: Such a threat is hardly barefaced

parts.words: Such a threat is hardly barefaced
parts.note: a threat that is hinted at rather than stated openly is figuratively covered, as a face behind a cloth is not bare

explanation.definitionFit: A veiled threat is concealed or implied, literally covered, hence not barefaced.

clue.text: Stopped and prepared a plan

definitions.meaning: halted, as a vehicle pulls to a stop
drafted or composed a scheme, as one draws up a contract

explanation.surface: Someone halted and worked out a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both came to a halt and drafted a document or scheme.

clue.text: How one danced when not quite sober

definitions.text: How one danced when not quite sober

parts.words: How one danced when not quite sober
parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance, and someone tipsy staggers about unsteadily, so one verb covers both the dancing and the drunken lurching

explanation.definitionFit: To reel is to dance a Scottish reel, and also to stagger as a drunk person does.

clue.text: The principle of no credit

indicators.note: of is read loosely as made of, so the letters of the words that follow are reworked into the answer

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rule saying nobody gets credit.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of NO CREDIT rearrange exactly into the answer; the setter offers only 'of' (made of) as the signal, an unusually weak one.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrine is a principle or body of teaching held as true.

clue.text: Service providing overhead savings for those in deep water

definitions.text: Service providing overhead savings for those in deep water

parts.words: Service providing overhead savings for those in deep water
parts.note: savings and overhead suggest finance and costs, but this is helicopters lifting people from the sea

explanation.definitionFit: This is the emergency service that saves people at sea, often by helicopter from above.

clue.text: Mild expletive used to replace an unprintable one

definitions.meaning: an old-fashioned genteel exclamation of annoyance

definitions.text: used to replace an unprintable one
definitions.meaning: printers set a short horizontal line in place of a swear word's letters, as in d—n

explanation.surface: A polite curse stands in for a rude one.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash is a gentle oath, and the printed horizontal line that stands in for a censored word.

clue.text: Nominally involved in a court case

definitions.text: Nominally involved in a court case

parts.words: Nominally involved in a court case
parts.note: someone named in legal proceedings, for instance as co-respondent in a divorce, has been formally referred to there by name

explanation.definitionFit: To be cited is to be named or summoned in legal proceedings.

clue.text: Country putting physical education before sport

indicators.note: before says the first piece is placed ahead of the second

parts.note: PE is the usual abbreviation for physical education, school games lessons
RU stands for Rugby Union, a sport

explanation.surface: A nation places school PE ahead of games.
explanation.definitionFit: Peru is a country in western South America.

clue.text: Female cotton spinner

definitions.meaning: a female donkey or wren is called by this name
the spinning machine invented by Hargreaves for cotton

explanation.surface: A woman who works at a cotton mill.
explanation.definitionFit: A jenny is a female donkey, and the spinning jenny was an early cotton-spinning frame.

clue.text: Sailor turned to crime, is seen in the dock

indicators.note: turned means the word for sailor is read backwards

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, a sailor
a sin is a wrongdoing or crime

explanation.surface: A seaman who turned criminal ends up in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the dock' looks like the courtroom dock; it is a dock for ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A basin is an enclosed area of water where ships are moored, a dock.

clue.text: Far better than other door-to-door salesmen?

definitions.text: Far better than other door-to-door salesmen?

parts.words: Far better than other door-to-door salesmen?
parts.note: a salesman going house to house who is miles in front of rivals is literally that far up the road; the idiom means much better

explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom means far superior to others, here taken literally as a long way up the road.

clue.text: Scores a goal, gaining England's final point

parts.note: to land a blow or a prize is to score it
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A team scores and so gets the decisive point.
explanation.walkthrough: LAND'S END is the westernmost tip of mainland England, in Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: Land's End in Cornwall is the extreme south-western point of England.

clue.text: A shy male sort of dog

indicators.note: sort is read as a verb, so these letters are sorted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A timid male is a kind of hound.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sealyham is a Welsh breed of short-legged terrier, a dog.

clue.text: Agitatedly anticipate bill coming in will cripple one

indicators.note: coming in tells us the bill is placed inside the shuffled letters
agitated letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: Nervously expecting a bill to arrive will leave one disabled with worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agitatedly' scrambles the given word into INCAPITATE before 'coming in' adds the account; 'will' and 'one' are only padding around the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To incapacitate is to disable or render powerless, much as crippling does.

clue.text: Support by arms or threaten by them

definitions.meaning: to raise and bear up with one's arms
to rob at gunpoint, the arms now being weapons

explanation.surface: Bearing something up, or menacing with guns.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold up is both to support and to rob at gunpoint.

clue.text: A cloister is more confined without it

indicators.note: without means the next piece is taken away from the first word

explanation.surface: A monastery walkway feels more cramped without its features.
explanation.definitionFit: Closer means more enclosed or confined, as a close atmosphere is stuffy.

clue.text: Just nothing left in New York

parts.note: nothing is zero, written O

indicators.note: in tells us the two pieces go inside the abbreviation for the city

explanation.surface: Nothing remaining in New York, merely.
explanation.definitionFit: Only and just are synonyms meaning merely or solely.

clue.text: Hunts — with seeming success

definitions.meaning: a hunt's gatherings of riders and hounds at a set place are its ...
the phrase ... with success means appears to succeed, so the word stands before 'with success'

explanation.surface: Fox hunts that look as if they are going well.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on the phrase 'meets with success'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunting meets are assemblies of a hunt, and one that meets with success succeeds.

clue.text: An image I'd behold in retrospect

parts.note: the contraction gives ID with the apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: looking back means the word for behold is read backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Gazing back at a picture of oneself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retrospect' turns only the old word for behold, giving OL; the contraction stays forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is an image or statue worshipped as a god.

clue.text: Fire an employee for drinking, perhaps

definitions.meaning: to dismiss someone from a job
an old name for a dry white wine from Spain, as Falstaff drank

explanation.surface: Dismiss a worker caught drinking on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack is to dismiss, and sack is an old sherry-like wine to drink.

clue.text: A bad start for one King of Mercia

indicators.note: the word for bad starts off, placed at the front of the other piece

parts.note: food gone bad has gone off

explanation.surface: A ruler of an Anglo-Saxon kingdom begins his reign poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercia was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom in the English Midlands; its king Offa built a famous dyke.
explanation.definitionFit: Offa was the eighth-century King of Mercia who built Offa's Dyke.

clue.text: Dispose of in haste

definitions.meaning: to deal with quickly or kill off
speed and promptness, as in acting with great efficiency

explanation.surface: Get rid of something in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispatch means both getting rid of something and promptness or speed in doing it.

clue.text: He's far out once more

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe giving no letter

explanation.surface: A man has wandered far away yet again.
explanation.definitionFit: Afresh means anew or once again, starting over.

clue.text: A roué in a bad mood gets the bird

indicators.note: in tells us the first pieces go inside the bad mood

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking, as in being in a pet
a rake is a dissolute man, a roué

explanation.surface: A sulking libertine is jeered at by the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the bird' looks like being booed off; the bird is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A parakeet is a small long-tailed parrot, a kind of bird.

clue.text: Haphazard arrangement of right and order

parts.note: taken as written
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A careless jumble of correct procedure and tidiness.
explanation.walkthrough: OM, the Order of Merit, is an honour awarded by the British monarch; 'arrangement of' is linking padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Random means without method or pattern, the same as haphazard.
